property: In MultiPartParser.parse, the filename derived from Content-Disposition must have HTML entities decoded (html.unescape) before any path-separator stripping occurs, and the resulting sanitize_file_name() output must reject '', '.', and '..' outright — sanitize_file_name(file_name) is the sole gate between the raw header value and file_name used by upload handlers.
vulnerability: MultiPartParser.parse called os.path.basename() on the Content-Disposition filename before html.unescape(), so an HTML-encoded path separator (e.g. '/') decoded after basename could reintroduce '/' and '.'/'..' were never rejected, letting attacker-controlled filenames like '..' or reconstructed traversal paths reach downstream upload handlers.

guard_lines: Sanitize the filename of an upload.
Remove all possible path separators, even though that might remove more
than actually required by the target system. Filenames that could
potentially cause problems (current/parent dir) are also discarded.
It should be noted that this function could still return un-sanitized
filenames if the remote user has proper permissions on the file system
to write to the target directory.

data.guard_summary: sanitize_file_name() unescapes HTML entities first, then strips everything up to the last '/' and '\', and returns None for '', '.', or '..', with parse() calling this method (aliased as IE_sanitize) before accepting file_name.

completeness.protected_value: the client-supplied upload filename parsed from the Content-Disposition header in MultiPartParser.parse (file_name)

uncovered.reason: This setter still runs os.path.basename() on the name assigned to UploadedFile.name, independent of the new sanitize_file_name gate. It's not in the scope of the F2 fix and doesn't unescape HTML entities, but since new_file() in TemporaryFileUploadHandler/InMemoryUploadedFile constructs UploadedFile with self.file_name (already sanitized), this consumer receives an already-sanitized value in the normal flow. However, if any other caller passes an unsanitized, HTML-encoded name directly to UploadedFile(name=...), basename() would run pre-unescape here, but this is outside the file_name flow controlled by the guard and not shown to be reachable with raw header data in the excerpts.

covered.reason: The sole point where the raw Content-Disposition filename is converted: 'file_name = force_str(file_name, encoding, errors='replace'); file_name = self.sanitize_file_name(file_name)' at lines 214-215, replacing the old os.path.basename()+IE_sanitize(html.unescape()) sequence. sanitize_file_name() now calls html.unescape() before rsplit('/') and rsplit('\\'), and rejects '', '.', '..'.

These consumers (new_file, TemporaryUploadedFile, InMemoryUploadedFile) all receive file_name only after MultiPartParser.parse has already called sanitize_file_name(), e.g. 'handler.new_file(field_name, file_name, content_type, ...)' at line 234, using the already-sanitized file_name from line 215.

completeness.value_note: Single value: the raw 'filename' from disposition.get('filename'), which after force_str is passed through sanitize_file_name() before being handed to upload handlers.
completeness.context_note: The fix diff and multipartparser.py excerpt fully show the guard applied at the only place the raw Content-Disposition filename is processed before being passed to upload handlers. uploadhandler.py and uploadedfile.py excerpts confirm downstream consumers receive the already-sanitized value from this single call site. No other file in the provided excerpts references or reprocesses the raw disposition filename, so coverage appears complete for the shown call graph.
